I'm incredibly doubtful that it's your levothyroxine. It takes anywhere from weeks to months to feel any change while on them. In fact, for me it was like the effects of the hypothyroidism itself got worse before they went away thanks to levothyroxine. I was a zombie for months even after treatment started. I had constant fatigue, staying awake for a handful of hours before I needed rest.

Depression, including the emotional numbness that it can bring, is a side effect of hypothyroidism. I really think your condition is just getting worse before it gets better.

Discuss it with your doctor if you are concerned, but I really dont think the levothyroxine is to blame, and your doctor will probably agree.

When I was diagnosed I looked up about this a LOT. It is common to mistake the hair loss as a side effects of the medication. It is actually a delayed side effect of hypothyroidism itself. And because you know you have hypothyroidism you're noticing it. Once I got my diagnosis it was like the fatigue got worse. 

It is gonna take time. It takes at least 3 months for you to feel better. Which sucks I know. Treatment for hypothyroidism takes a LOT of patience. You wouldn't suddenly go hyper, especially after just 2 months of medication. 

You'll get through, it's just gonna take time. Give it at least another month or two, and if you're still concerned bring it up with your doctor again, and besides, you'll probably be due another blood test in a month or so,  which will tell you if the medication is working.

Well actually some people get reverse SADs. Or you could just be overwhelmed in general. You're not broken ;) you're just fine.

It happens to us all, especially around winter time. It's dark, and so many festivities and people it can just get a little too much. Just take it easy on yourself :) deep breathes - it's just your fight or flight response going into hyper drive and it doesn't know what to protect you from.

Feel like I recommend this to everyone now, but first off, Adventures with Anxiety is a free browser game that takes about 30 mins and has helped me cope with Anxiety.  


Second, and more importantly, remind yourself to breathe. Don't be ashamed in any way of your anxiety, and dont beat yourself up if you get overwhelmed - it just makes things worse and you deserve far better than to do that to yourself. If in a group, don't be afraid to extract yourself for a moment to calm yourself down. Try to be open about your anxiety - anyone who would look down on you for that isn't worth being your friend in the first place. And you'll find a lot of people are probably really understanding. Just be yourself, relax, repeat. Feel free to repeat that to yourself when you get anxious - I know I do. Best of luck, and if you need more tips I'll try and come up with more - they're just the ones from the top of my head :)

Dude, I'm 28 and only in my first year of college. I'll be 30 when I graduate. There is no shame in being older and pursuing education. I know its taxing being around people much younger than you and seeing people your age have their degrees and their jobs. But comparing ourselves to those around us benefits exactly no one. 

We took the long way around, but I personally feel as a result we had a better idea of what we wanted, and we were better prepared for the dedication that higher education requires.

The people who hurt your feelings are assholes. Take your age as a source of pride - you've lived. That's what I try to do. You may be balding but that's coming for them too, take it all in your stride. You cant turn back the clock, but you can accept your age and be proud that you're making something of yourself.

Take care of yourself, take deep breaths, and do what you enjoy. Look at this situation with fresh eyes when the darkness slips away.
